package_info.package_manager: CDN (not a package manager, but a third-party hosted JavaScript service)
package_info.package_versions: All versions served after February 2024 (post-acquisition by Funnull)
package_info.why_malicious: The service was modified by new owners to inject obfuscated, dynamically generated malicious JavaScript into every website that included the CDN link. This code selectively targets users, evades detection, and can redirect users to malicious sites or potentially steal data, making every use of the CDN a supply chain attack vector.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when a user visits a website including the CDN script)
execution_context.file_location: Served dynamically from cdn.polyfill.io (injected into HTML via <script src="https://cdn.polyfill.io/v3/polyfill.min.js"></script>)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code checks the user agent and HTTP headers to identify mobile devices, avoids execution for admin users or when analytics are present, and after a delay, redirects the user to a malicious site. The payload is obfuscated and dynamically generated per request.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is served from a previously trusted CDN but now includes obfuscated logic, dynamic payloads, and selective targeting, all of which are classic indicators of malicious web supply chain attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal polyfill code should only provide JavaScript compatibility shims, not perform user agent checks, delayed redirects, or obfuscate its logic. Redirecting users or injecting third-party scripts is never expected from a polyfill service.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate uses of user agent checks and redirects exist in analytics or A/B testing, but never in a polyfill library or CDN context.
key_indicators: Conditional logic to evade detection (admin/analytics checks)
Served from a previously trusted but now compromised CDN

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when a user visits a website including the CDN script)
execution_context.file_location: Served dynamically from cdn.polyfill.io (injected into HTML via <script src="https://cdn.polyfill.io/v3/polyfill.min.js"></script>)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code injects a script tag pointing to a typosquatted Google Analytics domain, which then loads further malicious payloads or redirects the user to scam or adult sites based on geolocation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Injecting a script from a domain that closely mimics a legitimate analytics provider is a classic phishing and redirection technique. This is never expected from a polyfill service.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A polyfill service should never inject third-party analytics or redirect scripts, especially from typosquatted domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics scripts are only included intentionally by site owners, not injected by third-party polyfill services.
key_indicators: Redirection to malicious or scam sites

attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious JavaScript is loaded into every visitor's browser.

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript (snippet_1) executes in the user's browser, fingerprinting the environment and checking for mobile devices, admin users, and analytics.
attack_chain.leads_to: If conditions are met, proceeds to next step.

attack_chain.action: After a delay, the code either redirects the user to a malicious site or injects a fake analytics script (snippet_2).
attack_chain.leads_to: User is redirected to scam, betting, or adult sites, or further malicious payloads are loaded.

behavioral_signatures: Conditional execution based on user agent, admin status, or analytics presence
Delayed execution of redirects or script injections
Dynamic injection of scripts from typosquatted analytics domains
network_indicators: Redirects to domains associated with scams, betting, or adult content
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan web application source code and runtime DOM for references to cdn.polyfill.io. Monitor network traffic for requests to cdn.polyfill.io and typosquatted analytics domains. Use behavioral analysis to detect obfuscated JavaScript that performs conditional redirects or script injections, especially if triggered only for mobile users or after a delay. Flag any unexpected script injections or redirects originating from polyfill scripts.
